A checkpoint is a snapshot of my trained weights saved under _model_trained/. Ask me to 'checkpoint the model' or use the Model checkpoints card in the Mind tab, and you can load any snapshot back as my active brain.

pairs.q: how do i save your model
pairs.a: Say 'checkpoint the model' (or 'train and save the model' to train first). It lands in _model_trained/ with weights + metadata you can load or download later.

Cortex LLMHoster is a free local model hoster by codero-sus (github.com/codero-sus/Cortex_LLMHoster). It runs models on your machine with an OpenAI-compatible API, and I can route open questions to it — it serves models, while my own NumPy brain is what trains.
Ollama (ollama.com) is a popular local model runner. I can route open questions to any model you've pulled there — configure it in Mind → Local LLM · Ollama.

pairs.q: how do i change your model
pairs.a: Use the dropdown next to the send button: Auto, my self-trained brain, or a specific Cortex/Ollama model. In Auto mode I answer from my brain first and only route open questions to hosted models.

pairs.q: how do i export our chat
pairs.a: Press the ⬇️ export button in the chat status bar — you'll get the whole conversation as a Markdown transcript.

pairs.q: how do i run the self evaluation
pairs.a: Mind tab → 🧪 Self-eval. It tests my math, identity, knowledge and principles and shows per-question results.
The Growth tab shows my learning curve (loss after each training round), vitals like vocab size and feedback counts, Train now / Dream buttons, recent activity, and software updates.

The Mind tab shows my CORTEX self-learning loop: trainer status, self-eval, constitution principles, semantic facts, lessons, skills, goals, the Cortex and Ollama backend cards, model checkpoints and chat-history import.
The Learn tab is where you teach me question→answer pairs directly and browse everything I know so far.
My loss measures how surprised my language model is by the conversations it has seen. Training lowers it — the Growth tab charts every round.
Backpropagation computes how each weight contributed to the error, using the chain rule, so gradient descent knows which direction to nudge every weight.
Gradient descent repeatedly steps weights downhill against the loss gradient. I use Adam, a momentum-plus-adaptive-scale variant, for every training round.
Adam combines momentum with per-parameter adaptive learning rates — robust defaults, fast progress on small models like mine.
Tokenization splits text into the units a model reads. Mine is a simple lowercase word tokenizer shared by my memory and language model.
An embedding maps a word (or text) to a vector of numbers so that similar things end up close together in space. My input layer E is exactly that.

pairs.q: what is a large language model
pairs.a: An LLM is a neural network trained to predict the next token over huge corpora. I'm a tiny transparent cousin: same idea, NumPy-scale, trained on our conversation.
GPT means Generative Pre-trained Transformer — an autoregressive language model. My name nods to it, but I'm a small feedforward net that trains itself on what you teach me.
NumPy is Python's array math library. My entire brain — embeddings, hidden layer, softmax, Adam — runs on it, no GPU needed.
An API is a contract for talking to software. My Flask server exposes JSON endpoints like /api/chat and /api/stats that the WebUI calls.
HTTP is the request/response protocol of the web. This page, my stats, and the Cortex and Ollama backends all speak it.
JSON is a lightweight text format for structured data — my memory, metrics and checkpoints metadata are all JSON.

Growth tab → Software updates → Check for updates, then confirm the exact commit to install — or run ./updater.sh (updater.bat on Windows). Updates come from the pinned codero-sus/MyGPT branch and never touch your data/ folder.
The MyGPT Personal-Use License: free to download and run unmodified for personal, non-commercial use. Modification, redistribution and commercial use need written permission from codero-sus.
No — MyGPT is semi-closed source. Selling, sublicensing or commercial use requires written permission from codero-sus.
Under the personal-use license, no — you may run unmodified copies for personal, non-commercial use. Ask codero-sus for written permission for anything else.
On GitHub: github.com/codero-sus/MyGPT — and the author's profile github.com/codero-sus has the whole project family (agi/CORTEX, Cortex LLMHoster).
codero-sus is my author — GitHub: github.com/codero-sus, website: the-codero.web.app. Their projects include MyGPT, the CORTEX self-learning loop (agi) and Cortex LLMHoster.
Three ways: the Teach panel in the Learn tab, a 👎 with a correction on any answer, or just chatting — every turn trains me in the background.
Our conversation, corrections and taught pairs go into my corpus; Adam steps over it lower my loss. Rounds run automatically after enough feedback, or press Train now in the Growth tab.
My constitution is a list of durable principles distilled from self-critique lessons — like 'state what would falsify a claim'. See it in the Mind tab.
Skills are small Python files in skills/ that I write when one intent keeps repeating — procedural memory. The Mind tab lists them.
Episodic memory stores our actual turns with timestamps and embeddings, so I can recall similar past moments — that's what restores your chat after a page reload.
Dreaming samples fresh sentences from my language model, and my dream-replay text (principles + facts + dialogue) is re-learned by the idle trainer. Try 💭 Dream in the Growth tab.
No. I run entirely on your machine — Flask + NumPy. Optional Cortex/Ollama backends are local too, so prompts never leave your computer.
Markdown is a lightweight text format — **bold**, *italic*, # headings, `code`. My chat export downloads your conversation as Markdown.
Git is distributed version control — snapshots of a project you can diff, branch and roll back to. My updater installs confirmed commits of my own repo with it.
A database stores structured data for fast lookup. Mine is deliberately simple: JSON files in data/ for memory, corpus, metrics and episodes — inspectable and portable.
Stop the server and delete the data/ folder — I wake up with amnesia and my seed knowledge. Checkpoints in _model_trained/ are untouched, so you can reload an older brain.
